subject.title: fix(kill-tree): verify process group leader before using group kill to prevent gateway SIGTERM (#76259)

question: Should OpenClaw accept this PR's leader-verified direct-PID fallback for omitted `detached` Unix cleanup as the default safety behavior?
rationale: The code fix is coherent and proven, but it intentionally changes a shared process-cleanup default in a way that can trade descendant cleanup for avoiding gateway process-group termination when caller state is unavailable.

options.title: Accept Guarded Cleanup
options.body: Accept the current helper-side leader check, require the branch to be rebased and QA Smoke CI to be resolved, then land if the merge result stays equivalent.

options.title: Require More Caller State
options.body: Ask for additional explicit `detached` threading or tests for any caller maintainers believe must preserve group kill after leader exit.

options.title: Replace With Narrower Design
options.body: Pause this PR and sponsor a different process-cleanup contract if maintainers do not want omitted callers to fall back to direct-PID signaling.

recommendation.title: Accept Guarded Cleanup
recommendation.body: Accept the current helper-side leader check, require the branch to be rebased and QA Smoke CI to be resolved, then land if the merge result stays equivalent.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent process/agent-core ownership history and broad runtime refactor work make this the best available routing owner for the compatibility decision.
